short: Executed typing as the decoded action (M04) was ahead for MEG/EEG in 2025; keystroke-locked decoding (M06) and an n-gram LM (M07) are standard, and decoding needs known keystroke times.
position: The paper [@levy2025] changes the use-time action (M04): it decodes executed typing of memorized sentences from MEG and EEG, which no earlier MEG or EEG ledger paper does (Appendix), and the result repeats across 20 MEG and 20 EEG participants; that was ahead in February 2025. The decoder (M06) is standard: windows locked to known keystroke times are the field's usual segmentation, which the authors acknowledge as a limitation (Discussion); on the target's dataset, with encoders alone and no language model, the group's [later] asynchronous encoder gives CER 0.59 against 0.39 keystroke-locked, so timing a deployed system would not have carries much of the encoder's accuracy. An independent [later] control shows the aligned windows do not leak labels. The character n-gram language model (M07) is standard and corrects the typists' own errors against the intended sentence, with no language-model-only baseline. The signal is executed finger movement of healthy typists, so the paper demonstrates non-invasive keystroke decoding, not communication for people who cannot move; the two-fold MEG-over-EEG gain compares largely different cohorts.
